builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants
summary: The method replaces direct LLM prompting for noncoding variant interpretation with an agentic loop that separates deterministic DNABERT-based computation and database queries from LLM reasoning, adding a verifier and uncertainty-directed planning. It costs the infrastructure of 458 TF binding models plus access to ADASTRA, JASPAR, and ENCODE data sources, along with the engineering complexity of the planner-verifier loop. It can fail by abstaining when evidence is mixed or absent (three of four demonstrated TFs abstain), by inheriting false negatives from saturated binding models when no experimental data exists to rescue them, and its validation rests on a single variant locus.
rationale: This is a domain-specific genomics application rather than a generalizable inference or agent technique, and its abstention-heavy, single-locus evaluation does not establish transferable gains for a constrained-infrastructure production engineer.
technique: Evidence-constrained agentic loop for variant interpretation

claims.statement: The method replaces direct LLM prompting for noncoding variant interpretation with an agentic loop that separates deterministic DNABERT-based computation and database queries from LLM reasoning, adding a verifier and uncertainty-directed planning. It costs the infrastructure of 458 TF binding models plus access to ADASTRA, JASPAR, and ENCODE data sources, along with the engineering complexity of the planner-verifier loop. It can fail by abstaining when evidence is mixed or absent (three of four demonstrated TFs abstain), by inheriting false negatives from saturated binding models when no experimental data exists to rescue them, and its validation rests on a single variant locus.

The LLM planner reaches verdicts identical to a fixed-priority planner while making fewer tool calls, and the framework avoids hallucinated TF-binding claims by grounding all observations in real ADASTRA, JASPAR, and ENCODE queries; no quantitative factor is reported.
